key_insight: Data-free PINNs capture weak deep-cavity recirculation with floor-region velocity discrepancies below 5%, but accuracy depends on region and observable.
engineering_relevance: Assessing cavity-flow predictions regionally helps distinguish accuracy in weak recirculation zones from agreement in the stronger lid-driven flow.
method: Hard-constrained streamfunction PINNs for steady 2D incompressible flow at depth-to-width ratio 5.
Prescribed regional collocation and transferred initialization, with selected residual-scaling and envelope variants.
Validation against independent spectral/hp reference fields using the same Gaussian-regularized lid.
evidence_signal: Across Re = 100–1000, evaluation on a 121×605 grid found 5.130–7.850% interior velocity discrepancies; a separate 161×801 assessment at Re = 1000 reduced interior discrepancy from 5.624% to 2.658% with the refined workflow.
watch_item: Improvements compare accumulated finite-budget training workflows, not isolated sampling changes, and rotational-field discrepancies remain substantial.
paper_title: Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity
